newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Advertisers push for EU action on free speech.
newsitem.headline: Advertisers push for EU action on free speech.

text.p: The European Union should explicitly recognise the right to free commercial speech and adopt strict procedures for ensuring that advertising curbs are warranted, the World Federation of Advertisers (WFA) said on Monday.

The WFA, responding to a European Commission green paper on commercial communications, said EU governments should not be allowed to block material that is legal in other EU states and should rely on the industry to regulate itself.
"Advertisers have waited a long time for the single market to reach commercial communication," the WFA said in a statement.

"Many companies...now enjoy more freedom of movement of goods and services than ever before," it added. "However, the commercial communication that is necessary to support that free movement is tied up in national red-tape."

The WFA praised the Commission's paper, COM(96)192, for highlighting the barriers hindering advertising, direct marketing, sponsorship, public relations and sales promotions, but said its proposals did not go far enough.

The Commission proposed a mechanism, based on European Court of Justice case law, to help assess whether a market barrier to commercial communication was proportional to the objective it intended to achieve.
EU states would use the system to evaluate national measures and the Commission would use it to assess single-market complaints.

The WFA said the proposal should be strengthened to require governments to notify the Commission before adopting restrictions on commercial communication, giving interested parties a chance to comment.
A decision about whether the measure is "proportional" should be made within three months, it said.
The EU should also strengthen its system for taking legal action against governments that violate single-market principles, it said.

The WFA said it would also ensure that a self-regulatory structure is set up in each EU state outlining sanctions and consumer safeguards. Consumer complaints would in the first instance be referred to the existing cross-border regulatory system operated by the European Advertising Standards Alliance, it said.
The advertisers said their proposals aimed to ensure that any commercial communication that was legal in one EU state would be permitted across the Union.
